thread:
incident-bot: PAGER DUTY · P1 triggered · high 5xx rate · service=inference-realtime-prod · region=us-west-2b

carla: i'm oncall, acked PD. starting triage.

carla: quick snapshot — ELB target group shows ~30% unhealthy targets, upstream 502/503 surge. dashboards: tokenization and model-host errors spike at same time.

bob: i can see a pattern in host logs — sidecar HTTP calls to 169.254.169.254 are timing out intermittently. a bunch of sidecar threads hang waiting on IMDS -> kills healthcheck responses.

alice: wow, IMDS timeouts? that usually indicates instance metadata path/networking issues in AZ. any ENI errors from cloudwatch?

carla: checking VPC/ENI metrics now. there's a small bump in RT for dhcp/metadata and some ENI RX drops in us-west-2b.

dave: customer-facing: a few customers report 503s and model failures. support dashboard shows ~12k failed requests last 10m, about 18% of traffic for that region.

sre-manager: label impact: partial regional degradation, not full region down. escalate if cross-AZ fallback not stabilizing in 15m.

carla: mitigation plan attempt 1: drain the most affected instances from the ELB target group so traffic shifts to healthy targets in other AZs. doing a controlled drain of 5 instances.

bob: FYI draining is fine but sidecar hangs might cause ongoing tokenization failures on the healthy pool if the same AMI is used. recommend we also toggle fallback routing policy to prefer other AZs for 10m.

carla: toggling route weighting in Route53 to shift 80% traffic away from us-west-2b -> applied. verifying DNS propagation.

incident-bot: DeployGate: Route53 change propagated to EDGE in ~3m.

alice: while traffic drains, let's run the IMDS health runbook on a sample host: SSH -> curl -s -D- "http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/" -m 2 -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n". need someone to run across 3 hosts.

bob: i'm running it now on infra-azb-12/14/19. results: 504, 504, 200. so it's intermittent across instances.

carla: can we restart the sidecar on the 504 hosts without rolling the instance? safer to avoid stop/start.

bob: sidecar restart initiated via systemctl; logs show immediate recovery of health endpoint. but after ~7m one host went back to 504 on metadata checks.

dave: support note — temporarily added a region notice: "Experiencing elevated errors in us-west-2b; traffic being shifted. We'll update in 15m."

support-bot: message sent to status page subscribers for affected endpoints.

alice: hypothesis: metadata path to IMDS is being delayed by degraded AZ fabric (DHCP/metadata proxy), causing long blocks in processes expecting immediate metadata — those block healthchecks -> ELB marks unhealthy.

carla: action item: coordinate with AWS? open a ticket/console case for us-west-2b networking flaps. i'll submit with all ENI metrics + sample curl timeline.

carla: temporary mitigation 2: change ELB health check grace to increase threshold (raise healthy threshold and interval) to avoid flapping until AWS confirms. pros/cons? buys time but could mask real host failure.

sre-manager: do it for a short window (10-20m) while we continue triage. document exact change for rollback.

bob: changed target group health check: interval 30s -> 10s? wait that's backwards. set unhealthy threshold to 5 -> 10 and healthy threshold to 5 -> 3. made change and saved. note: these values differ per TG.

carla: monitoring: error rate fell from 18% to 6% in 8m after traffic shift + targeted restarts + healthcheck tweak. latency still a bit high for some requests.

alice: continuing to collect evidence: packet drops, ENI metrics, and IMDS trace logs. if AWS confirms AZ-level control-plane strain, we should plan cross-AZ failover for longer duration.

dave: impacts: several enterprise customers observed degraded throughput and ~15-30s tail latencies. none reported persistent data loss. billing/usage unaffected. support will prepare targeted outreach for customers with high error volumes.

incident-bot: Oncall Handoff reminder: carla -> next oncall (eve) at 04:00 UTC. please include actions taken and outstanding items.

carla: i'm summing up for handoff: 1) route53 weight shift applied (80% away from us-west-2b), 2) drained 5 worst hosts, 3) restarted sidecars on 3 hosts, 4) increased unhealthy threshold temporarily, 5) AWS case opened (case# 1234567890). ongoing: AWS investigating AZ fabric/metadata path. watch dashboards for IMDS 5xx and ELB target unhealthy.

alice: adding runbook entry: if IMDS timeouts persist -> schedule rolling replace of affected instances with new ENI attachments (ASG instance refresh with new launch template that forces new ENI allocation) rather than rebooting in-place.

carla: support message updated on status page with ETA: "Monitoring. Traffic shifted; remediation in progress. Next update in 30m."

bob: logs & artifacts uploaded to S3 path: s3://redwood-incident-artifacts/2775001234/ (attached to AWS case).

dave: preparing customer follow-up template for account execs. will include timeline, mitigation steps, and expected next steps once AWS confirms root cause.

carla: ok handing over to eve for night coverage. last check: error rate stable ~5% vs baseline <1%. if error rate >10% escalate to P1 all-hands.

incident-bot: Handoff completed. next_oncall: eve.

carla: thanks team. i'll be reachable if we need context. posting postmortem stub in #postmortems with links to artifacts and runbook edits.

sre-manager: good containment. after AWS response, we'll do a follow-up postmortem to decide permanent mitigations (IMDS client backoff, region routing defaults, and ASG refresh policy).

support-bot: closed few duplicate tickets and linked affected tickets to the incident.

carla: thread closed for active triage — will reopen if AWS provides new info or errors spike.
notes: post-incident: runbook updates required for IMDS timeout detection and ASG refresh guidance
